fix_subject: fix another vector index bug ... grrr
defect: The new GetDataOwnership only flushes the append state but never unpins the KEEP_EVERYTHING_PINNED partitioned data before handing it off, so the transferred data stays pinned in memory and cannot be spilled.
The new GetDataOwnership flushes the append state but never unpins the partitioned data, so the handed-off collections stay fully pinned (KEEP_EVERYTHING_PINNED) and cannot be evicted.

fix_subject: Removed faulty default param
defect: The Windows ListFiles definition repeats the default argument FileOpener *opener = nullptr already given in the header declaration, which is ill-formed and fails to compile with MSVC.

The Windows out-of-line definition of LocalFileSystem::ListFiles repeats the default argument 'FileOpener *opener = nullptr' that the header declaration already has, a redefinition of a default argument that fails to compile.

fix_subject: Fixes for single-file compilation
defect: The new inline virtual GetStatistics returns unique_ptr<BaseStatistics> in a header where BaseStatistics is only forward-declared, so translation units without base_statistics.hpp fail to compile in the single-file build.
The new inline virtual GetStatistics returns unique_ptr<BaseStatistics> in a header where BaseStatistics is only incomplete, which breaks single-file compilation.

fix_subject: Fix for Python 2
defect: The new HUGEINT fetch passes a const char* from c_str() to PyLong_FromString, whose Python 2 signature takes a non-const char*, breaking the build against Python 2.
The new HUGEINT fetchone path passes a const char* to PyLong_FromString, which takes a non-const char* on Python 2, so the Python 2 build fails to compile.

fix_subject: Fixes for amalgamation build
defect: This commit adds a relation-API class duckdb::JoinRelation that clashes with the optimizer struct duckdb::JoinRelation, which its new EXPRESSION_GET branch also uses, breaking the amalgamation (single translation unit) build.

This commit adds a relation-API class named JoinRelation in the duckdb namespace that clashes with the optimizer's struct JoinRelation used here (including the newly added EXPRESSION_GET branch), breaking the amalgamation build.

fix_subject: fix tests with left and right joins
defect: The new LeftRightOptimizations swaps the children of ANY_JOINs regardless of join type (breaking LEFT any-joins) and flips LEFT comparison joins to RIGHT even when a right_projection_map exists, which is then not swapped.

LeftRightOptimizations swaps the children of any LOGICAL_ANY_JOIN regardless of join type (breaking LEFT/SEMI any joins) and flips LEFT comparison joins to RIGHT even when a right_projection_map is set.

fix_subject: fix tests with left and right joins
defect: The rewritten pass-through loop uses while (OperatorNeedsRelation(op->type)) where the original condition meant the opposite, so it walks through projections and gets and stops at operators it should pass.
The rewritten pass-through loop uses 'OperatorNeedsRelation(op->type)' where the old code continued while the operator was NOT one of those types, inverting the condition.

fix_subject: fix bug in the AddColumnIds method
defect: In the new AddColumnIds the parameter column_ids shadows the member, so column_ids = std::move(column_ids) self-assigns the parameter and never sets the member.
In the new AddColumnIds the parameter column_ids shadows the member, so 'column_ids = std::move(column_ids)' self-assigns and the member is never set.

fix_subject: fix some issues
defect: HandleStructExtract computes the extracted field type by walking indexes from front to back, but the recursion stores the outermost extract first, so nested struct extracts get the wrong field type or index into the wrong struct children.

The new field-type computation walks indexes from indexes[0] (the innermost field) on the column's top-level struct type, the reverse of the nesting order, giving the wrong type or an out-of-range child.

fix_subject: Fix alignment issues
defect: The new Slice/SliceInPlace API reads at target_offset and writes at source_offset (roles swapped), and its Vector::Slice callers pass end instead of end - offset as count, so the mask is oversized and the source validity is read past its end.
The new SliceInPlace writes at source_offset+i and reads at target_offset+i (roles swapped), so Slice with a non-zero source offset writes past the new mask and copies the wrong bits.

fix_subject: leak
defect: The change calls the new Utf8Proc::Normalize(const char*, size_t), which returns a malloc'ed char*, and converts it straight into a std::string without freeing it, leaking memory for each non-ASCII string.
The change calls the char*-returning Utf8Proc::Normalize(data, len) and converts the result to std::string, leaking the malloc'ed buffer on every call.

fix_subject: Fix #8624 - allow changing of schema and search_path parameters even if configuration is locked
defect: The new lock_configuration check rejects every RESET, including schema and search_path, so locking the configuration also breaks schema switching (USE and RESET schema).
The new lock_configuration check rejects RESET of every option, including schema and search_path, which USE and normal session work depend on (issue #8624).

The new duckdb_string_t_data takes duckdb_string_t by value and returns a pointer into it, which dangles for inlined strings once the call returns.

The change replaces '#if defined(_WIN32) && !defined(__MINGW32__)' with '#ifdef _WIN32' for DUCKDB_API, so MinGW builds now get dllimport/dllexport and fail.

fix_subject: fix: description returns an optional too
defect: GetDescription's return type was narrowed from py::object to py::list although the implementation returns py::none() when there is no result, so conversion of None to a list raises instead of returning None.
GetDescription's return type becomes py::list although the implementation returns py::none() when there is no result, so description raises instead of returning None.

fix_subject: fixing result offsets for selection vector calculation and filter interaction
defect: ConvertDictToSelVec dropped result_offset, so defines and filter are indexed from 0 although define_out is filled at define_out + result_offset, reading wrong defines/filter bits when a read spans several pages.
ConvertDictToSelVec drops result_offset and indexes defines and the filter by row_idx alone, so dictionary pages read at a non-zero result offset use the wrong define levels and filter bits.

fix_subject: fixed issue I caused
defect: TableBinding::Bind asserts D_ASSERT(entry) in debug builds although a table binding may have no catalog entry (e.g. table functions), so debug builds fail the assertion.
The new debug block asserts D_ASSERT(entry) in TableBinding::Bind although bindings without a standard entry are legal, so debug builds abort.

fix_subject: Fix several race conditions around statistics updating
defect: The new public ColumnData::statistics member is merged by concurrent appends and updates (and later read) without any lock, a data race.
The new public, unsynchronized ColumnData::statistics is merged by concurrent appends and updates and read elsewhere without a lock, a data race.

fix_subject: Fix several race conditions around statistics updating
defect: DataTable::GetStatistics copies columns[column_id]->statistics without a lock while appends and updates merge into it concurrently, a data race.
The new DataTable::GetStatistics copies columns[column_id]->statistics without a lock while other threads merge into it.

fix_subject: Fix install extension at version
defect: TransformVersionNumber reads Child<IdentifierParseResult>(1) although the grammar rule VersionNumber <- Identifier has a single child, so installing an extension at a version fails.

TransformVersionNumber reads Child<IdentifierParseResult>(1) of a list, which does not match the grammar 'VersionNumber <- Identifier' added in the same commit, so INSTALL ... VERSION is not transformed correctly.

fix_subject: fix parenthesis
defect: Adding the cast moved a parenthesis, turning pow(2, n - 1) into pow(2, n) - 1, so the debug assertion on per-neighbor subset counts fails.
Adding the cast moved the parenthesis, so the assertion compares against pow(2, n) - 1 instead of pow(2, n - 1) and fails in debug builds.

fix_subject: More testing and bug fixing related to the csv line reporting on parallel mode
defect: The generic search for the failing row was commented out and line_error is only computed for comma-separated floats, so cast errors in other paths (e.g. date format) report the line of the chunk start.
The change removes the per-row scan that located the failing row and sets line_error only in the comma-separated float cast, so date-format (and other) cast errors report the batch start line.

fix_subject: More testing and bug fixing related to the csv line reporting on parallel mode
defect: GetLine clears current_batches, so after one error every other erroring thread passes CanItGetLine and computes its line while earlier batches are unfinished, hitting the 'Missing batch index' InternalException or reporting inconsistent lines.
LineInfo::GetLine now clears current_batches, so a second erroring thread passes CanItGetLine early and computes its line from incomplete lines_read, giving a wrong line or 'Missing batch index'.

fix_subject: More testing and bug fixing related to the csv line reporting on parallel mode
defect: LineInfo keeps no record of an error already reported, so when an earlier batch throws without finishing, a later erroring thread spins forever in CanItGetLine.
The new LineInfo has no record of an error already reported, so when an earlier batch's thread throws without leaving current_batches, a later erroring thread spins forever in CanItGetLine.

fix_subject: fix the issues with unrecognized or faulty submitted named parameter values
defect: ToNamedParameters emits option names 'skip_rows', 'date_format' and 'timestamp_format' that the CSV option parser does not recognize ('skip', 'dateformat', 'timestampformat').
The new ToNamedParameters emits keys read_csv does not accept or misreads ('skip_rows', 'date_format', 'timestamp_format'), so ReadCSVRelation's re-bind fails or loses options.

fix_subject: fix the issues with unrecognized or faulty submitted named parameter values
defect: Feeding every named parameter to SetReadOption fails for options it does not handle (columns, names, types, all_varchar, file options), raising unrecognized-option errors.

The new loop feeds every user option through SetReadOption, which does not handle options such as columns, names, types, all_varchar or normalize_names, so they are rejected or ignored before sniffing.

fix_subject: fix some more tests, add some more. can only push down fiters on windows if all window expressions have the filtered column in the partition
defect: PushdownWindow pushes a filter below the window as soon as it is on the partition of any one window expression, although it must be on the partition of every window expression, giving wrong results with differently partitioned window functions.

The new PushdownWindow pushes a filter below the window when it matches the partition of any single window expression (and FilterIsOnPartition is a stub returning true), which is wrong when other window expressions are not partitioned on that column.

fix_subject: Fix linking issues in R package
defect: The change removes AppendBoolean and declares the primary Append<T> template without a definition or a bool specialization, so Append<bool> as used by the R package fails to link.
The templated Append is declared without a primary definition and with no bool specialization (plus a duplicate double declaration), so calls such as Append<bool> fail to link (R package).

fix_subject: Bug fixing
defect: The rewritten GetChunkInternal advances lhs_idx before the RHS matches of the current key are exhausted (and again via the for loop) and does not reset rhs_chunk for a new LHS chunk, so matches pair with the wrong LHS row or are lost.

The rewritten GetChunkInternal advances lhs_idx in the for loop and after a full result even while the current key's RHS chunk or leaf scan still has matches, pairing remaining matches with the wrong LHS row; rhs_chunk is also not reset per LHS chunk.

fix_subject: fix progress test by initializing variables
defect: total_cardinality and cur_rows_read are declared uninitialized and compared after the loop, which is undefined behaviour and a spurious failure when the loop body never runs.
The test reads the uninitialized total_cardinality and cur_rows_read after the loop when the loop body never ran (undefined behaviour, spurious failures).

fix_subject: fix; remove reference to StandardError
defect: RegisterExceptions imports the Python 2 'exceptions' module and its StandardError, which do not exist in Python 3, so module initialization fails.
RegisterExceptions imports the 'exceptions' module and its StandardError, which exist only in Python 2, so module initialization fails on Python 3.

fix_subject: fix list resize and first aggregate
defect: In the sort-key FIRST/LAST Update, is_null is read with validity.RowIsValid(assign_sel[i]) without mapping through idata.sel, so NULLs are misdetected for dictionary or sliced input.
In the new sort-key FIRST/LAST Update, the second loop checks validity at assign_sel[i] without mapping it through idata.sel, so NULLs in non-flat inputs are detected wrongly.

fix_subject: fix list resize and first aggregate
defect: The default-value copy fills a selection with default_idx, already resolved through the default vector's own selection, and passes it to VectorOperations::Copy on the unflattened vector, applying the selection twice.

The default-value copy builds its selection vector from default_idx, already resolved through the default vector's own selection, and VectorOperations::Copy applies that selection again, so non-flat default vectors yield wrong values.

fix_subject: fixed wrongful assertion + missing ORDER in test
defect: The added D_ASSERT(flag_bytes != 0) fails for a group with a single value, whose first value carries no flag, so debug builds abort.
The change adds D_ASSERT(flag_bytes != 0) in FlushGroup, which is false for a group holding a single value (no flags written), so debug builds abort on valid data.

fix_subject: fix another bug with held pins
defect: Next() passes collection.segments[current_segment_idx] to FinalizePinState after NextScanIndex has already advanced current_segment_idx, so pins are released or stored against the wrong segment when the end lies at the start of the next segment.
Next passes collection.segments[current_segment_idx] to FinalizePinState after NextScanIndex has already advanced current_segment_idx, so the pins go to the wrong (or out-of-range) segment.

fix_subject: Fix for race condition in parallel index test
defect: The new parallel-append test expects COUNT(*) to equal i+1 in each thread although other threads' committed inserts are visible, so it fails spuriously.
append_to_primary_key_with_transaction checks that the table count equals its own i+1 while other threads insert concurrently, so the test fails spuriously.

fix_subject: fix null value
defect: The new EnumTypeInfoTemplated constructor checks validity.RowIsValid(i) instead of RowIsValid(idx), testing the wrong row for non-flat vectors.
The new EnumTypeInfoTemplated constructor checks validity at i instead of the selected index idx.

fix_subject: Fix for #5566
defect: The new conditions 'column > 0 || try_add_line' at a newline and in final_state never add a row for a single-column CSV, where column is always 0, so its rows are merged or dropped.
The parser now adds a row at a newline only if column > 0 or try_add_line, and the final state likewise, so single-column CSVs never emit rows or lose their last value (#5566).

fix_subject: Avoid underflow in max_row initialization from resulting in an incorrect max_row setup
defect: max_row = MinValue(count, parent.max_row - start) underflows when the row group starts beyond parent.max_row, so the row group is scanned fully instead of not at all.
'state.parent.max_row - this->start' underflows when the row group starts beyond parent.max_row, so MinValue returns count and rows past max_row are scanned.

fix_subject: Fixing issue with erroring maximum line size
defect: The refactor checks the sniffer's own error_handler for MAXIMUM_LINE_SIZE instead of best_candidate->error_handler, so the maximum line size error is never raised.

The rewrite calls ErrorIfTypeExists(MAXIMUM_LINE_SIZE) on the sniffer's own error_handler instead of best_candidate->error_handler, so maximum-line-size errors recorded by the best candidate are no longer raised.
